data.narrative:
Oxford Quantum Circuits is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $350M to date. The broader quantum computing sector comprises 11 peers—3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, Infleqtion, and others.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a $595M implied valuation, applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement to the $350M raised proxy. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable; while 6 quantum computing peers exist, insufficient narrow-stage comparables (fewer than 3 same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with similar valuation tiers) preclude reliable median derivation without introducing bias from all-sector medians.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $506M to $684M, centered on $595M. This single-method estimate carries material uncertainty. Key risks include: dependence on a stage-progression heuristic rather than market-derived peer multiples; absence of comparable Series C quantum computing transactions to validate the 1.7x multiplier; and sector-wide uncertainty around path to commercial returns and competitive positioning among fragmented hardware architectures. The narrow methodological basis suggests sensitivity to stage-up velocity assumptions and calls for validation through additional comparables as the market matures.
